record.name: Wisconsin Well Woman Program
record.administeredBy: Wisconsin Department of Health Services (delivered through county and tribal coordinating agencies)
record.summary: Free breast and cervical cancer screening for women with little or no health insurance. It pays for mammograms, Pap tests, pelvic and clinical breast exams, HPV tests, and follow-up diagnostic testing.
record.benefit: Payment for covered screening and diagnostic services with no premium, deductible, or co-payment, when you use a provider enrolled in the program.

steps: Find your county or tribal Well Woman coordinating agency.
Contact that agency to enroll and confirm income eligibility.
Get screened by a provider enrolled in the program.

of._sourceText: Are a woman between ages 40 and 64
Meet income requirements (at or below 250% of the federal poverty level)
Don't have health insurance, or / Have insurance that doesn't include routine check-ups and screenings. / Aren't able to pay the deductible or co-payment.
Are a woman between ages 40 and 64 [plus] exceptions to the 40-64 age group

of._note: AGE_BANDS today are under-60 / 60-64 / 65-plus. This rule needs a 40 floor and a 64 ceiling, neither of which any current band expresses.

of._sourceText: 65 or older and not eligible for Medicare or if you can't afford Medicare Part B

of.note: 35-39 only qualifies through specific clinical routes (Family Planning Only enrollment + referral after an abnormal exam, or self-reported breast symptoms, or cervical screening only). Not decidable from interview facts.

unencodable: The 35-39 age band's three clinical entry routes (referral after an abnormal breast exam/mammogram; self-reported breast symptoms; cervical-screening-only) -- these turn on a clinical event, not a fact a person can self-report reliably in an interview.
'not every medical provider offers every service' -- provider-network availability varies by county.
The precise income figures live in a separate PDF (P-43029) refreshed annually; only the 250% FPL rate is on the page.

surprises: This one rule needs six facts that do not exist, and one of them (a real age with a 40 floor and 64 ceiling) breaks the current age model outright -- AGE_BANDS' coarsest band 'under-60' swallows the entire 40-64 window, so `age` cannot even approximate the rule. A sex/gender fact ('isWoman') is also new and politically load-bearing.
